content:
maria (partnerships): FYI VendorX started sending nightly usage batches from their APAC gateway. payload contains local timestamps (JST) and occasional rows with usage = 0. These 0 rows are creating entitlement churn when our TTL window runs out. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:
aj (eng): can you paste a sample payload? is there an idempotency key or batch id we can use to dedupe?
maria (partnerships): here's a redacted sample they sent (they said it's what their SI SDK emits):
```json
{"customer_id":"c-123","timestamp":1672531200,"region":"ap-northeast-1","usage":0,"metering_id":"m-789"}
{"customer_id":"c-123","timestamp":1672534800,"region":"ap-northeast-1","usage":120,"metering_id":"m-790"}
```
aj (eng): thanks. that timestamp looks like epoch seconds but they told us they use local tz when constructing it — so it can be off by +9h depending on client clock.
danielle (billing): the problem for finance: 0-usage rows flip entitlements in our daily rollups and then downstream invoice rules mark credits/zeros. We need stable decisions or we'll hit incorrect credits for customers.
lee (si): vendorX SI confirmed some devices batch when offline. they emit a placeholder row with usage=0 to indicate heartbeat, not billable. they do not add a consistent batch_id.
aj (eng): proposed steps: 1) treat usage=0 as non-billable but persist raw event for QA (flagged) 2) require conversion of timestamps -> UTC at ingest (assume epoch is local; if region in APAC, convert by -9h) 3) add soft dedupe window: if same customer+metering_id within 24h, keep last non-zero and mark earlier zeros as heartbeat.
maria (partnerships): that would work. can we do a quick ingestion patch on staging and run vendor sample? @ops-bot can you spin a staging run? :pray:
ops-bot: Deploy job queued: deploy/ingest-vendorx-staging -> started (job id: deploy-4421).
aj (eng): sample ingest transform (pseudo):
```yaml
ingest_transforms:
  - name: normalize_ts_to_utc
    when: payload.timestamp_exists
    action: convert_epoch_local_to_utc
  - name: heartbeat_filter
    when: payload.usage == 0
    action: flag_as_heartbeat(not_billable=true)
  - name: dedupe_by_metering_id
    window: 24h
    action: collapse_keep_last_non_zero
```
lee (si): will ask VendorX to start sending a batch_id in next SDK patch (ETA 2 weeks). meanwhile we'll rely on customer+metering_id dedupe.
danielle (billing): for accounting: we need a reconciliation tag on flagged events so ledger can ignore them in daily aggregation. add field: reconciliation_reason=HEARTBEAT.
aj (eng): will add reconciliation_reason and a ledger-safe boolean. also adding a metric: flagged_heartbeat_count per customer for two weeks so finance can review.
maria (partnerships): assign tasks: @aj implement staging transform & metric (due EOD tomorrow), @lee get vendor to add batch_id (ETA update by Fri), @danielle confirm ledger ignore rule and sign-off once we see staging data.
danielle (billing): ack. i'll also run a retrospective on past 30 days to see how many credits were affected and estimate exposure.
ops-bot: deploy/ingest-vendorx-staging -> success (job id: deploy-4421) in 00:03:12.
aj (eng): patched staging, ran sample, results: 12 heartbeat rows flagged, dedupe collapsed 3 duplicate groups, metrics emitted to infra.metrics.vendorx. leaving logs here: https://staging-logs/internal/deploy-4421 (internal).
lee (si): vendor patched SDK roadmap item, they'll try to backfill batch_id for future releases. they can't retroactively add batch_id to old devices.
maria (partnerships): ok next steps: 1) run 30-day replay with transform in staging and produce a ledger delta report for @danielle (due Wed) 2) schedule quick customer comms template in case any legit usage was suppressed (likely rare) 3) monitor flagged_heartbeat_count -> if >1% of daily usage, escalate.
danielle (billing): noted. if staging replay delta > $5k/mo we escalate to partnerships and legal for customer notice.
aj (eng): I'll open a follow-up thread with replay results. closing this thread once ledger delta report uploaded. :white_check_mark:
maria (partnerships): thanks team. great fast turnaround. :tada:
